source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 5 (Geomorphic Processes).

sections.heading: 1. Endogenic and Exogenic Processes
points: **Geomorphic processes** shape the Earth's surface, driven by **endogenic (internal)** and **exogenic (external)** forces.
**Endogenic processes** — powered by Earth's internal heat: **diastrophism** (folding, faulting — orogeny/epeirogeny) and **volcanism** (movement of magma). They build relief.
**Exogenic processes** — powered by the Sun and gravity: **weathering, erosion, transport, deposition**. They wear down relief (**gradation**).

sections.heading: 2. Weathering
points: **Weathering** = the in-situ (on the spot) breakdown of rocks (no movement).

sub: **Physical/mechanical** — frost action, thermal expansion, unloading, salt crystallisation.
**Biological** — action of plants, animals and humans.

points: Weathering prepares material for erosion and helps form **soils** and enrich **ores**.

sections.heading: 3. Mass Movement and Erosion
points: **Mass movement (mass wasting)** — downslope movement of material under **gravity** (landslides, slumping, creep, flow) — no transporting agent needed.
**Erosion** = removal + transport of weathered material by agents (running water, glaciers, wind, waves, groundwater).
**Deposition** = laying down of eroded material.
The overall levelling of the land is called **gradation** (degradation = wearing down; aggradation = building up).

sections.heading: 4. Soil Formation
points: **Soil** forms from weathered rock (parent material) + organic matter over time.
Factors: **parent material, climate, relief (topography), organisms, time**.
Soil-forming processes and horizons (profile) develop gradually.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Endogenic = internal forces (diastrophism, volcanism) → build relief.
Exogenic = external forces (weathering, erosion, deposition) → wear down relief.
Weathering = in-situ breakdown (no movement); physical/chemical/biological.
Mass movement = downslope under gravity (no agent).
Soil factors: parent material, climate, relief, organisms, time.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Weathering has NO movement** (in-situ); **erosion involves transport**.
**Endogenic = internal (build up)**; **exogenic = external (wear down)**.
**Mass movement** is driven purely by **gravity** (no transporting agent).
**Oxidation and carbonation** are types of **chemical** weathering.
